purpose: Record what System Master is expected to contain and what boundaries must remain true, without converting historical planning claims into current implementation standing.

architecture_expectations.requirement: SYSTEM MASTER is the product root/system-of-systems.
CORE provides the shared Foundation & Spine consumed by product tools; tool systems do not duplicate Core authority silently.
LEARNING is a first-class tool system inside SYSTEM MASTER.
BOOK is a first-class end-to-end tool system inside SYSTEM MASTER.
PROSE is a child system of BOOK and owns Book Evaluator/evaluation and prose-training intelligence without self-authorizing BOOK canonical writes.

operating_expectations.requirement: Every executable work item has an explicit owner path, current control head/watermark, completion delta, evidence expectation, stop condition and next-state rule.
No newer branch/chat/workflow/ticket becomes authority merely because it is newer.
Completed work is append-only evidence; current state selects from it but does not rewrite it.
Unallocated work may be inspected but may not execute, schedule, promote or redefine architecture until an owner is assigned.
Second Shift executes only live delegations revalidated against the current system control head; stale delegated work is superseded before execution.

historical_product_module_inventory.source: System Master Foundation & Spine Forensic Audit and Workload Hardening Study, 2026-08-31, section 3.3
historical_product_module_inventory.historical_statement: The audit tracked 40 product capability modules. Its old implementation-status counts are historical and must not be reused as current status without present evidence.
historical_product_module_inventory.allocation_rule: Owner hints are not implementation proof. Each module requires a current-state census and an explicit owner/capability registration before new execution if not already covered by a canonical control record.

change_rule: New product expectations require an explicit registry entry with owner and standing. If an expectation changes, supersede it; do not erase the prior expectation from history.
